subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martins <sofia.martins@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Sofia 
 great to connect today. Thanks for walking us through AcmeCloud's planned 1.0 rollout and the performance expectations. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can get you an accurate Dedicated sizing estimate:

Summary of what you gave us on the call:
- Primary use case: contextual customer support (multi-turn chat) + summary generation for transcripts.
- Expected TPS (text generation requests): 12 TPS peak for chat flows, with spikes up to ~20 TPS for batch jobs.
- Typical prompt: concatenated context + 1-2 user messages, average prompt length ~600 tokens; expected average response ~160 tokens (token mix ~80% short chat, 20% longer summarization).
- Concurrency target: 120 concurrent sessions (most idle waiting for user, ~30% active token generation at any time).
- SLO: 95th percentile tail latency <= 250ms for short chat completions; longer summaries okay up to 1.2s.
- Data residency: US (VPC), sensitive PII redaction required.

Clarifying questions:
1) Are the 12 TPS steady-state or measured during business hours only? You mentioned heavy night-batch jobs 
 can you share expected off-hour TPS?
2) For the models: you indicated wanting a multi-model strategy (gpt-like open 13B for most chat, a 70B variant for high-quality summaries). Can you confirm which model families you prefer (e.g., LlamaX, Redmond-13B) and whether quantized variants are acceptable for savings?
3) Any strict GPU preference (A100 80GB vs H100) or are you open to Redwood recommending based on cost/latency tradeoffs?

Next steps: we'll assemble a Dedicated sizing draft with two options (performance-optimized H100 cluster and cost-optimized A100-heavy pool) + estimated monthly cost and expected latency/TPS headroom. I'll include a short benchmark appendix with token mix assumptions and concurrency modeling.

I'll aim to send the draft by Friday (2026-08-13). If you can answer the questions above by tomorrow, that will help tighten the estimate.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood-capacity-quicklist.pdf (see note in attachments)

From: Sofia Martins <sofia.martins@acmecloud.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Thanks Rafael 
 appreciate the clear recap. Quick replies below:

1) 12 TPS is our expected peak during business hours PST (08:00-18:00). Off-hours steady-state for background jobs is ~3
5 TPS, but we do weekly batch runs that briefly spike (up to 20 TPS) for transcript summarization.
2) Model family: we prefer to start on an open-family equivalent to LlamaX-13B for chat. For summaries, we want higher quality -> LlamaX-70B or comparable. We're open to 4-bit quantization on 13B; for 70B we'd prefer FP16 unless the quality regression is measurable.
3) No hard GPU requirement 
 cost is a factor. We'd like your recommendation based on our SLOs.

Also FYI 
 security is requesting that any on-prem/VPC option include KMS integration and audit logs. We expect to evaluate Dedicated first; Private VPC only if there are compliance blockers.

Happy for you to send the draft Friday.

Sofia
Sofia Martins | Head of Platform Engineering | AcmeCloud

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: AcmeCloud sizing assumptions

Rafael / Aditya 
 leaving a short note while you finalize the draft for Sofia. Based on the call notes and Sofia's replies, my suggested baseline assumptions to include in the deck:

- Traffic shape: business-hours peak 12 TPS sustained, background 3
5 TPS, weekly burst to 20 TPS for 30
45 minutes.
- Token mix: prompt avg 600 tokens, response 160 tokens -> average total 760 tokens per request. For sizing, model 80% chat (shorter tails) and 20% long summaries (up to 1k tokens).
- Concurrency: 120 sessions, assume 30% of sessions active producing tokens concurrently -> 36 concurrent generation jobs.
- Buffer/overprovision: recommend 1.5x headroom for spikes (so plan capacity for ~54 concurrent token-generating jobs).
- Model choices: 13B quantized for chat; 70B FP16 for summaries.

Attachment: I drafted two sizing options in a quick spreadsheet (attached) and a short note on expected cost +/- 20%. Rafael, if you want, I can attach the benchmark CSV and the draft estimate to the email to Acme.

Marissa
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: AcmeCloud sizing assumptions 
 technical notes

On our sizing assumptions: adding the technical detail we'll include in the appendix so Sofia sees the modeling rationale:

1) GPU baseline options (per-node effective throughput estimates for their token mix):
   - A100 80GB (FP16 / 4-bit quant): ~5500 tokens/sec per GPU for LlamaX-13B quantized (chat workload), ~1400 tokens/sec per GPU for LlamaX-70B FP16 (summaries).
   - H100 80GB (FP16): ~8500 tokens/sec per GPU for 13B, ~2500 tokens/sec per GPU for 70B.

2) Concurrency and batching: continuous batching will improve GPU utilization. For 36 concurrent active jobs (avg), with token generation rate targets we model two cluster options:
   - Cost-optimized: 4 x A100 80GB nodes dedicated to the 13B chat fleet (plus 1 A100 for fallback summaries) -> estimated steady throughput ~20k tokens/sec aggregate; supports the 12 TPS steady-state with ~2x headroom for short chats.
   - Performance-optimized: 3 x H100 nodes for mixed workload -> aggregate ~30k tokens/sec; this gives better tail latency and headroom for spikes/batch compaction.

3) Expected latency projections (short chat ~160 tokens gen):
   - A100 option: p50 ~90ms, p95 ~260
320ms (depends on batching window).
   - H100 option: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~150
200ms.

4) Recommendation: present both options. If Acme prioritizes strict p95 < 250ms for short chats, recommend H100 cluster. If cost matters more and p95 up to ~300ms is acceptable, go A100 with optimized batching and a conservative autoscale policy.

I've attached a small CSV with micro-benchmark runs (gpu-benchmarks-2026-08.csv) and the rough cost model. Rafael 
 I left a few TBDs on concurrency multipliers; suggest we surface these to Acme as assumptions and request a short traffic sample (1 week) if they want a refined model.

Aditya
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

 which works best?

 attaching the files now.
